title: USPS Proposes Permanent Fuel Surcharge for Ecommerce Sellers
summary: USPS proposes an 11% fuel surcharge for January 2027. See how ecommerce sellers can review shipping costs and compare their carrier options.
body_markdown:
The United States Postal Service (USPS) has[proposed](https://about.usps.com/newsroom/national-releases/2026/1112-usps-recommends-shipping-price-adjustments-for-2027.htm) a permanent 11% fuel surcharge for domestic packages from January 17, 2027, subject to Postal Regulatory Commission review.


The proposal covers USPS Ground Advantage, Priority Mail, Priority Mail Express, and Parcel Select. It would replace April’s temporary 8% transportation increase. USPS also proposes separate base rate increases averaging 5.9% for these services.


The fuel surcharge excludes international shipments, although USPS has separately proposed international rate increases.


Although[October’s announcement](https://www.supplychaindive.com/news/usps-to-debut-weekly-fuel-fee-in-2027-matching-fedex-ups-practices/872778/) described weekly fuel adjustments, the[November filing](https://prc.arkcase.com/api/prc-dockets/filing/downloadFile?fileId=258184\&inline=true) specifies a fixed surcharge initially. USPS intends to introduce weekly adjustments later in 2027 and plans to review the surcharge in July.


For ecommerce sellers, these proposed changes affect shipping budgets and the cost of offering free delivery. The impact on individual orders depends on the service used, package characteristics, and applicable pricing.


Sellers can compare total shipping costs across carriers using recent orders, including surcharges. Review shipping charges and free delivery thresholds against those calculations and check how your shipping software handles fuel surcharge updates. Compare equivalent delivery services when assessing your carrier options.
